neighbours.label: The article right after 'in'/'dans' in a recipe step, where a cooking vessel (saucepan, bowl, kettle, skillet) is about to be named; quiet on 'in a' in non-cooking sentences and on recipe steps without 'in a'.
fire: Chop the onions and cook them gently in a skillet with a little butter.
Combine the flour, salt and yeast in a large mixing bowl.
Place the potatoes in a pot of cold salted water and bring to a boil.
Melt the chocolate in a small saucepan over very low heat.
Heat the milk in a pan until it just starts to steam.
Faire fondre le beurre dans une poêle à feu moyen.
Toss the salad leaves with the dressing in a wide bowl.
Simmer the stock in a heavy pot for about forty minutes.
quiet: My cousin lives in a flat above the bakery on the main street.
She studied in a library downtown until late every evening.

He grew up in a village at the foot of the mountains.
Preheat the oven and line the tray with parchment paper.

predictions: median fire ~0.5 (probes: in a saucepan 0.74, in a kettle 0.75, dans une casserole 0.43, in a large bowl 0.29); near misses < 0.04 (lives in a house 0.003, works in a bank 0.003, cooking class in a center 0.007, Grease a baking dish 0.03).
short: 'in a' before a cooking vessel in a recipe
notes: A next-token predictor of cookware: the logit effect of the + pole promotes tablespoons/cup, and the - pole fires on the article before the vessel.
